defects: Frame 3 is almost empty: one stray, half-rendered grey 'B' glyph floats top-right while the title builds in. It looks like a broken text animation, not a designed beat.
Black-tea disc hatching: thin diagonal lines show moiré and stair-stepped edges at 100%. The hatch also runs through the leaf's translucent green, so the leaf reads as dirty, not overprinted.
Leaf vein strokes stop short of the leaf edge and overshoot unevenly. Thin white strokes are aliased on the diagonals.
Within each 1/6 s pair, the hero objects barely change (a few degrees of rotation, a slight scale). Motion is mostly a slow drift, with no anticipation, overshoot or weight.
End card holds about 6.9 s while the only things that change are the caption fading from grey to black and the logo appearing. That is dead air against a 1.5 s benchmark.
Mid-fade 'Ethiopia Guji · washed' sits in low-contrast grey on off-white. It is close to illegible in the poster frame.
Mottled 'texture' fills are a large-scale noise overlay with no light or falloff. They read as a filter, not as print or material.
gaps: Transitions: each note (bergamot, black tea, peach) is a separate card swap. Top work would morph one disc into the next, for example the citrus wheel rotating into the hatch and the leaf, then the three discs physically pouring into the cup, so the Venn becomes the brew rather than a static diagram.

Timing and arc: energy peaks early and repeatedly (change spikes at 3, 6 and 8–9 s), then dies into a long static end hold. There is no build to a peak at around 70% and no designed release. The tail needs to land in under 2 s, with the steam loop and logo hit timed to the 12.3 s drop.

Finish and sound: hatch moiré, aliased hairlines, ghost-glyph frames and a flat noise overlay keep it at template level. The soundtrack is dense and produced, but it is a steady pluck/percussion loop. Apart from the 12.3 s break, no sound design voices the objects (citrus cut, leaf rustle, pour).
